trajectory.patch:
The error is caused by an incorrect device initialization order in the `power_management_1cpu` test. The test logic assumes an initialization order of `device_a` -> `device_b` -> `device_c`, but the device definitions result in an order of `device_a` -> `device_c` -> `device_b`. This discrepancy leads to a failed assertion when checking device power states during suspend/resume operations.

The fix is to swap the initialization levels of `device_b` and `device_c` to match the order expected by the test logic.

tests/subsys/pm/power_mgmt/src/main.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
DEVICE_DT_DEFINE(DT_INST(1, test_device_pm), NULL,
		PM_DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_INST(1, test_device_pm)), NULL, NULL,
		POST_KERNEL, CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE,
		NULL);
========
DEVICE_DT_DEFINE(DT_INST(1, test_device_pm), NULL,
		PM_DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_INST(1, test_device_pm)), NULL, NULL,
		PRE_KERNEL_2, CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEVICE,
		NULL);
